Assessment and Late Submission Guide
Students should upload coursework through the learning portal before the deadline shown on the course page. Late submission is normally penalized according to the assessment instructions. A student who becomes ill may request an extension, but medical evidence must be provided before the original deadline. The request should be sent to the course coordinator and should clearly mention the affected course, assessment title and requested extension period. An extension is not automatic and should not be assumed until the coordinator confirms it.

Students should keep a copy of the submitted file and check that the portal displays a successful upload message. The accepted file format for this example is PDF. If the portal is unavailable, the student should take a screenshot of the error and contact the help desk before the deadline. Sending a file to a classmate does not count as an official submission.

A change in personal plans is not the same as illness and does not create an automatic exception. The medical-evidence condition remains part of the illness rule. Students should read the current course instructions because dates and assessment requirements can change. This document is synthetic teaching material and is not an actual university policy.
password:
Student Account and Password Help
A student who forgets an account password can start recovery from the login page by selecting the recovery link. The system will ask for the registered email address or another approved account detail. Follow the instructions sent by the service and create a new password that is not used on another website. Never share a password or recovery code with another person.

If the recovery email does not arrive, check the spam folder and confirm that the correct email address was entered. Wait a few minutes before requesting another message. Repeated requests may make the process confusing. If the account remains inaccessible, contact the IT help desk and provide the student username, but never send the password itself.

A password reset is different from creating a new student account. Students should not create a second account to avoid a login problem because records may become separated. The help desk may ask for identity confirmation before making an account change. This guide describes a sample process only; actual services may use different screens and security checks.

Coursework Upload Instructions
Coursework should be uploaded through the assignment page in the learning portal. Open the correct course, select the assessment, and read the submission instructions before choosing a file. For this example, the final assignment must be saved as a PDF. Check the filename and open the PDF once before uploading so that missing pages or unreadable content can be noticed.

After selecting the file, wait for the upload to finish. A successful submission should show a confirmation message or receipt. Students should keep the receipt until the assessment has been marked. Uploading a draft to a personal cloud drive does not submit it to the course. If the wrong file is uploaded, check whether the portal allows replacement before the deadline.

If the upload page gives an error, record the time and take a screenshot. Contact the help desk or course coordinator promptly. Do not assume that an email attachment will replace the official portal submission unless the course coordinator confirms that arrangement. This is a synthetic example and does not replace current course instructions.
contractor:
Remote Work and Contractor Conditions
This sample workplace guide explains the difference between employee and contractor arrangements. Employees may request remote work when their manager approves the arrangement and the work can be completed safely away from the office. Approval may depend on the role, schedule, equipment and business needs. A request should describe the proposed working days and how communication with the team will be maintained.

Contractors have a separate condition. Contractors may work remotely only when the signed contract explicitly permits remote work. A general statement about employee flexibility does not automatically apply to contractors. If the contract is unclear, the contractor should ask the contract owner or the responsible manager for written clarification before working remotely.

The same rule should be checked against the correct contract version and dates. A verbal comment should not be treated as a replacement for the signed terms. This document is synthetic training content, not legal advice or an actual company policy. It demonstrates why retrieval systems should keep eligibility rules and exceptions together and should preserve the audience field when searching.
printer:
Printer Troubleshooting Guide
When a printer has power but produces blank pages, first check that the paper tray contains suitable paper and that the printer display shows no warning. Check the ink or toner level using the printer controls or the computer's printer utility. A very low or empty cartridge can cause pages to appear blank. Follow the device manual when handling cartridges and do not force a part that does not move easily.

If ink or toner is available, run the printer cleaning utility. The cleaning process may use some ink, so follow the on-screen instructions and avoid repeating it unnecessarily. After cleaning, print a test page to see whether the text appears. If the test page is still blank, check that the correct printer is selected and that the document itself contains visible text.

A scanner producing a blank image is a different problem. Check document placement and the selected scanning source for a scanner issue. Do not apply scanner instructions to a printer fault just because both problems involve blank output. If the printer still fails, note the model and contact technical support. This is a general synthetic guide; the device manual takes priority.
